record.paper_title: SOFT PHYSICS AND INTERMITTENCY : OPEN QUESTION(S) in KRAKOW
record.original_question: Is the proposed micro-universe picture of multiparticle production correct, in which dynamical fluctuations originate from partons structuring themselves during scattering into colorless clusters through rearrangements until hadrons form in the new vacuum structure?

evidence.quote: In the Micro-Universe represented by a production of particles from the vacuum, it is tempting to find the origin of dynamical fluctuations in the structuration of partons during the scattering process.
Fluctuationg structures are formed, rearrangements occur, till they succeed to form new objects, the hadrons, which are required by the new vacuum structure.
Is this picture right or wrong?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In high-energy hadronic and nuclear collisions, the final state consists of a large number of produced hadrons whose multiplicity distributions exhibit non-trivial dynamical (non-statistical) fluctuations, often quantified by scaled factorial moments F_q(δ) = ⟨n(n-1)...(n-q+1)⟩/⟨n⟩^q computed in phase-space bins of size δ. An "intermittent" behaviour corresponds to a power-law growth F_q(δ) ∝ δ^{-φ_q} as δ → 0, with positive intermittency exponents φ_q.

Consider the following proposed dynamical mechanism (the "micro-universe parton-structuration picture") for the origin of these dynamical fluctuations:

(i) During a scattering process, partons (quarks and gluons) created from the vacuum undergo a self-structuration phase, forming transient fluctuating color configurations.
(ii) These fluctuating structures undergo successive rearrangements, organizing partons into colorless clusters.
(iii) The process terminates when colorless clusters condense into hadrons, consistent with the asymptotic (confining) vacuum structure of QCD.
(iv) The dynamical fluctuations observed in factorial moments (intermittency, multifractal scaling of hadron multiplicities in phase-space) arise precisely from this parton structuration / rearrangement / hadronization cascade in the vacuum.

Question: Is this proposed mechanism a correct description of the origin of dynamical multiplicity fluctuations and intermittency observed in soft multiparticle production? Specifically, can one derive (or rule out) the observed power-law scaling of factorial moments and multifractal spectra from a dynamical model based on parton structuration into colorless clusters and rearrangement towards hadrons in a non-perturbative vacuum?
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the physical correctness of a conjectured picture of soft multiparticle production. No definitive verification or refutation appears in the literature; intermittency in soft hadron production remains an active topic and competing models (cascading, QCD parton showers, Bose–Einstein correlations, critical-fluctuation pictures) coexist without consensus.

status_evidence.title: Intermittency in particle physics (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of intermittency and multiparticle correlations, noting that the dynamical origin of factorial moment scaling in soft processes is not uniquely determined.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing dynamical pictures for intermittency exist; no consensus on the underlying mechanism.
